evidence.label: mcp-python-ssrf-metadata-endpoint (medium/low)
evidence.detail: Listed, not deducted: this check is new and its precision has not been measured, so it is shown for review and scores nothing. A string literal names the cloud instance-metadata endpoint, which serves a hosted instance's credentials to anything on it that asks. Code that contacts it can be the last step of an SSRF; the same literal is also how an SSRF defence names what it blocks, and a pattern cannot tell the two apart, so this is listed for review and not deducted.

evidence.label: authentication_model
evidence.detail: stdio transport: the client launches the server as a subprocess, so the OS process boundary is the auth boundary — `03` §4 does not penalise absent auth here

evidence.label: transport_security
evidence.detail: declared transport: stdio — launched as a subprocess by the client, so the security boundary is the client process, not a network port (`03` §4)

evidence.label: secret_handling
evidence.detail: detect-secrets matched 20 credential-shaped string(s), every one from a keyword or entropy heuristic (Base64 High Entropy String, Secret Keyword). Those flag placeholders, variable names and content hashes as readily as credentials, so they do not establish the committed credential `03` §4's 0 asserts, and this sub-check is not scored; Secret Keyword at evalview/chat.py:580; Base64 High Entropy String at evalview/cloud/client.py:13; Secret Keyword at evalview/commands/init_cmd.py:1074; Secret Keyword at evalview/core/llm_configs.py:58; Secret Keyword at evalview/core/llm_configs.py:65; Secret Keyword at evalview/core/llm_configs.py:72; Secret Keyword at evalview/core/llm_configs.py:79; Secret Keyword at evalview/core/llm_configs.py:86; Secret Keyword at evalview/core/llm_configs.py:93; Secret Keyword at evalview/core/llm_configs.py:100; …and 10 more matches

evidence.label: authorization_granularity
evidence.detail: no tool registration was recognised anywhere in the source. An MCP server registers tools by definition, so this is a gap in our detection rather than a server with none, and `03` §4's threshold cannot be applied to it. A tool-list handler IS present, so the tools are built in a shape this counter could not enumerate.

evidence.label: bus_factor
evidence.detail: this repository's 12-month history is longer than the bounded walk `04` §7 performs, and the authors found so far span more than one of `03` §5's bands. A limit of ours, not a finding about the server.

evidence.label: repository_signals
evidence.detail: `03` §5 scores this by quartile WITHIN the server's category, which needs a distribution across every scanned server and so cannot be computed while scanning one. It is a post-pass over the crawl and that pass does not exist yet.
